UPSTREAM: ASoC: da7219: Add common clock usage for providing DAI clks Reland commit 6b27cd601234e ("BACKPORT: FROMGIT: ASoC: da7219: Add common clock usage for providing DAI clks") The difference is that now we are using component in codec driver. There is a need to use DA7219 as DAI clock master for other codecs within a system, which means that the DAI clocks are required to remain, regardless of whether the codec is actually running playback/capture. To be able to expose control of the DAI clocking the common clock framework has been employed. The current implementation adds a simple clock gate for enabling and disabling the DAI clocks, with no rate control supported (this is still handled through standard hw_params() functions as before). If DT is enabled then the clock is added to the OF providers list, otherwise a clkdev lookup is used. Signed-off-by: Adam Thomson <Adam.Thomson.Opensource@diasemi.com> Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit fc8f7ea2d6c074baaad202c9187962bfa493ef13) BUG=b:80592327, b:73825035 TEST=ARCH=arm64 make allyesconfig; CROSS_COMPILE=aarch64-cros-linux-gnu- ARCH=arm64 make -j64 Signed-off-by: Cheng-Yi Chiang <cychiang@chromium.org> Change-Id: I2f58c04569fffc763033fceb0bee6b18a74c45ba Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1139724

UPSTREAM: ASoC: da7219: clkdev_drop usage depends on CONFIG_COMMON_CLK Fixes: ASoC: da7219: Add common clock usage for providing DAI clks clkdev_drop usage in the codec remove function should be dependent on if CONFIG_COMMON_CLK is defined for the platform, otherwise it can cause build failures for platforms that do not support this. The clkdev_* functions are still defined for those platforms, in headers and source but the functions are not linked in. This patch resolves this issue, so clkdev_drop is only used if CONFIG_COMMON_CLK is defined. CHROMIUM: Move some of the netfilter-related modules to in-kernel Some of the iptables-restore scripts performed by Android expect some netfilter modules to be already loaded. For instance, the script: *mangle -A tetherctrl_mangle_FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN SYN \ -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu COMMIT First checks if the "mangle" table is already loaded[1]. If it isn't, it tries to load the "ip6_tables" ko[2] and checks for the table again (since the Android config has all the netfilter modules built-in)[3] without explicitly trying to load the relevant ko ("ip6table_mangle"). This causes the whole operation to fail without attempting to actually run the command (which would have resulted in the kernel loading the kernel by itself). To avoid the above issue, and to also avoid sprinkling `modprobe` commands all around the system (since Android runs in a container without the CAP_SYS_MODULE capability), this change moves the netfilter-related modules from being as a module to being built in-kernel if they: * Appear in the android-base.cfg list[4]. * Have the CONFIG_NETFILTER_XT_*, CONFIG_IP_NF*, CONFIG_IP6_NF_* prefixes. * Are not explicitly loaded through other means (which exclude CONFIG_IP_NF_NAT, CONFIG_IP_NF_TARGET_MASQUERADE, CONFIG_IP6_NF_FILTER). 1: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/iptables/+/master/\ iptables/ip6tables-restore.c#297 2: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/iptables/+/master/\ libxtables/xtables.c#418 3: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/iptables/+/master/\ iptables/ip6tables-restore.c#67 4: https://android.googlesource.com/kernel/configs/+/master/\ android-4.4/android-base.cfg BUG=b:68277526 TEST=The above iptables-restore script now succeeds TEST=third_party/autotest/files/site_utils/bootperf-bin/bootperf seconds_power_on_to_login: before: 9.61 (avg, over 10 runs) after: 9.587 (avg, over 10 runs) Signed-off-by: Luis Hector Chavez <lhchavez@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/747003 Reviewed-by: Kevin Cernekee <cernekee@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit 617f812275dcf2f0d62e42850bf8c4683d991cc6) BUG=b:111852346 BUG=b:111883508 Change-Id: If2b17832802b08aeeb4a7cd96f915068f2536117 Signed-off-by: Hugo Benichi <hugobenichi@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1156195 Commit-Ready: Hugo Benichi <hugobenichi@google.com> Tested-by: Hugo Benichi <hugobenichi@google.com> Reviewed-by: Luis Hector Chavez <lhchavez@chromium.org>

image_tool: add rma_metadata.json This file is added to RMA image under cros_payload folder to track number of boards and their corresponding install shim partitions. For example, a new created RMA shim with only one board should have rma_metadata.json as: [{"board": "BOARD", "kernel": 2, "rootfs": 3}] And when multiple RMA shim are merged by 'rma-merge' command, the metadata will be updated, e.g. [{"board": "BOARD_A", "kernel": 2, "rootfs": 3}, {"board": "BOARD_B", "kernel": 4, "rootfs": 5}, ] BUG=chromium:866810 TEST=manual test TEST=make test Change-Id: Ib64cc0e13842f988e7ac23e98f69d88bab552450 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1148304 Commit-Ready: Wei-Han Chen <stimim@chromium.org> Tested-by: Wei-Han Chen <stimim@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org>

The original branch provided by Intel (Luca Coelho) is at branch core35-for-chromeos-4.4 on https://git.kernel.org/cgit/linux/kernel/git/iwlwifi/chromeos.git and has been mirrored as intel-wifi/v4.4-core35 on cros.
